assessments.explanation: The court dismisses the application for judicial review.
The applicant arrived in Canada in 2011 and submitted a refugee claim shortly after.
The Board rejected the claim on credibility grounds, finding no risk if returned to China.
The Board found the applicant fabricated his story based on several adverse credibility findings.
The Board gave little weight to the applicant’s evidence due to credibility concerns.
The court reviews the reasonableness of the Board’s plausibility findings based on the evidence and context.
The court emphasizes the deference owed to the Board’s expertise and fact-finding role.
The court finds the Board’s conclusion about the applicant’s risk based on his age and actions reasonable.
The court notes that the Board’s failure to mention specific evidence does not imply error.
The Board’s negative credibility assessment was reasonable given the evidence about police practices.
The Board was entitled to infer from the applicant’s ability to leave China that he was not under persistent pursuit.
The court adopts the reasoning that fabricated stories support the conclusion of a fraudulent claim.
The court finds the Board’s sur place assessment was thorough and reasonably reasoned.
